key_insight: Computational rheometry supports improved vane-in-cup conversion relations, with the 24-arm fractal vane producing nearly axisymmetric yielding that better approximates circular Couette flow.
engineering_relevance: Improved torque-to-stress and rotation-to-strain-rate conversions can make rheological measurements of yield-stress materials more accurate.
method: Model viscoplastic fluids using the Herschel–Bulkley constitutive law.
Simulate 2D flow with augmented Lagrangian finite elements and 3D flow with regularised finite volumes.
Compare conventional 4- and 6-arm vanes with a 24-arm fractal vane.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive 2D and 3D simulations across a broad parameter range, but provides no quantitative accuracy gains or experimental validation.
watch_item: Circular Couette conversions can be inaccurate for non-axisymmetric yielding; revised closures require validation for the intended geometry and operating conditions.
paper_title: Three-dimensional computational rheometry of viscoplastic fluids in vane-in-cup fixtures
